entries.title: a context provider that runs out of time runs again on the next index
entries.summary: A context provider past its time budget used to be skipped for that pass and never run again for the files an incremental pass leaves alone, so what an index held depended on how busy the machine was. The index now records the cut, and the next index over the whole tree re-parses every file so the provider runs again; partial passes keep the record. The steering hooks also recognise a search over a whole drive, and the published package no longer spells a code-execution call it doesn't make. SECURITY.md names LSP enrichment as the one opt-in path that can run repository code.

entries.title: a session lists only its own workspace's indexes by default
entries.summary: `list_repos` shows the indexes whose folder is the server's working directory, inside it, or containing it, and says how many it hid. A bare name that matches several indexes picks the one in the workspace. An exact `owner/name` or a path still loads any index, and the `cross_repo` tools are unchanged. A server started in the home folder, above it, at a filesystem root, or where no index lives lists everything and says so. `"repo_visibility": "all"` restores the old listing. It scopes what a session is shown, not who can read.

entries.title: environment variables stay supported, and no longer warn that 2.0 removes them
entries.summary: The config loader no longer logs "Deprecated: ... will be removed in v2.0" when a `JCODEMUNCH_*` variable fills a key the config file leaves unset, and CONFIGURATION.md documents env vars as a supported fallback (a config file value still wins). No 2.0 is planned. `JCODEMUNCH_SHARE_SAVINGS=0`, the documented opt-out from anonymous savings sharing, keeps working. A test fails if a loader message or a tracked doc promises a 2.0 removal again.

entries.title: git blame is off by default, and it no longer adds "2 properties" to a file summary
entries.summary: Indexing no longer runs a timed `git log` on every git repository by default: `git_blame_enabled` defaults to `false`, and an existing config that sets the key keeps its value. With it on, the provider runs as before minus the "2 properties" suffix it added to every file summary it covered. SECURITY.md now lists it, since it stores commit authors' names in the index and, with AI summaries on, sends them to the summarizer. Search ranking doesn't move.
